attitudeTravel.scope: Actual quaternion increments in the previous body frame. Signed/absolute axis travel is not an Euler angle or proof of a clean single-axis 360-degree maneuver.

method: At each actual integrator slice: rotate every delivered nozzle force into world coordinates, divide by actual body mass, separate gravity, remaining applied aerodynamic forces and Cannon linear damping, then compare with the real velocity increment. Integrate each contribution through the same semi-implicit position update. This is force accounting, not a counterfactual trajectory where other forces were removed.
limits: Both full-turn comparisons deliberately start at 120 m and use bench external supply. No ground-start or finite-gas maneuver success is inferred.

The before solver is the frozen 3.15 implementation with current shared helper dependencies. In this collision-free reference there is no contact refinement or tyre force, so the force objective change is isolated.

The original negative body-Y request remains desiredWrench and contributes to the reported allocation residual. Only the ordinary pilot-rate allocation objective changes its unreachable negative lift component to zero.
Required attitude torque can still entail down-facing main-jet thrust while inverted. There is no invented negative lift actuator, increased force limit or direct pose correction.
The candidate spends more total gas in this comparison. Improved attitude allocation and reduced inversion duration are a tradeoff, not a claim of universally faster or more economical flight.
